coverage_decomposition_2025.note: new-entrant WAR is covered by the ETA-prospect block and the recentering remainder; the original level gap was the exposure-floor universe (see retro_backtest)

calibration.kind: v2: per-team sub-floor depth pool + uniform remainder to the 2,430-win league sum, applied per season; the cohort intercepts (side x age band, retro-backtest-fit 2022-24) lost their holdout gate and are not applied
limitations: depth-pool team assignment needs a contract row; unassigned depth WAR rides the uniform remainder
spread stays projection-compressed (correct for a mean projection; bands carry the uncertainty)

forward_gate.scope: first season only; 2028+ are not gateable
forward_gate.metric: MAE vs actual wins; baseline = prior-season wins carry-forward

design.no_lookahead: curves + WAR map refit per target on data through Y-1 (Gate-1 pattern)
design.team_assignment: primary actual season-Y team by exposure stint (B-Ref war_daily); isolates engine error from roster churn - disclosed
design.population: every player with >=1 input season in Y-3..Y-1; absent target season scores actual WAR 0; new entrants (rookies/IFA, ~61 WAR/season) are outside the veteran engine and absorbed by the recentering level

player_level._reading: pooled mixes rostered players with players who never took a roster spot (actual WAR 0 by construction); assigned_only is the population the team roll-up is built from and is the one to quote

ship_decision.challenger: cohort intercepts (side x age band) + recentering
ship_decision.served_vector_note: served_recentered scores the vector proj_export actually serves today, which the challenger-vs-incumbent comparison does not. A served arm that matches 'recentered' means the vector is doing nothing; worse means it is actively costing wins.

multi_year.kind: controlled-core: each player counts only through his control window (_last_controlled_season); each season is independently recentered to the 2,430-win league sum
multi_year.display_metric: the surface shows year-1 W-L + WAR plus lockedPct = WAR-weighted control share (controlled / everyone-stays WAR over 2027-31); aging cancels, so it isolates cost control
limitations: only the first season (2027) is forward-gateable; out-years (2028+) are a controlled-core competitive trajectory, NOT scored against actual standings

the cliff is Spotrac signed_through where present, else an age-based proxy (no service time in the pipeline). It is NOT the club control window on the players board, which is the salary path's own end (ctrlThru)
cohort intercepts were fit on year-1 residuals; out-year application re-bands by age but is an approximation

window_alignment.kind: surplus-weighted farm ETA (etaMean) vs the controlled-core WAR center (coreCenter); etaAlignYears = etaMean - coreCenter, <= 0 = farm arrives inside the controlled-core window (aligned). That window is the age-proxy cliff (_last_controlled_season), not the club control window the players board prints
window_alignment.weight: expected surplus $ (value_mm), floored at 0; count-weight fallback
limitations: etaMean is surplus-weighted by the platform surplus model (its uncertainty flows through); coreCenter is the controlled-core trajectory, not a scored contention forecast
orgs whose farm carries no positive-surplus prospect fall back to a count-weighted center and report no arrival curve

serve_vector_tripwire.question: does the served vector read worse than plain recentering on the holdout retro fold
serve_vector_tripwire.vector_note: the cohort-intercept vector does not serve; served_recentered scores the vector as it stood when proj_backtest last ran (2026-08-04), and the live roll-up is the plain recentered arm
serve_vector_tripwire.source: retro_backtest.ship_decision.holdout_mae (proj_backtest.py; preserved across re-exports; flag is None when the block is absent)
